bp.title: Content pipeline
bp.sub: How many articles a day, what to write next, what waits in review and which old articles need a refresh.
bp.off: The pipeline is off: the calendar fills each day to its own target ({n} a day). Below is what the pipeline would do; switch it on in its card.
bp.readOnly: You can see the pipeline. Changing its card needs the permission to publish.
bp.reason_off: The pipeline is off, so the calendar's own target counts.
bp.reason_notStarted: Nothing is live yet: the start pace counts from the first live article.
bp.reason_starting: Starting: the full pace begins on {d} if the journal is healthy then.
bp.reason_full: Full pace: the journal is healthy.
bp.reason_held: Held at the start pace: the journal is not healthy right now (see below). It goes up again by itself when it is.
bp.backPct: Sent back in review: {p}% (healthy up to {max}%)
bp.backNone: No review answers yet in this time.
bp.idx_low: Google indexing: too few articles indexed.
bp.idx_unknown: Google indexing: not known yet (Search Console is not connected), so the full pace waits.
bp.idx_skipped: Google indexing: not checked (the card says not to wait for it).
bp.flowSub: Each step opens its own page.
bp.buffer: Ready ahead: {have} of {want} articles ({d} days at today's pace).
bp.bufferShort: Finish {n} more to fill {b} days ahead.
bp.nextSub: Approved topics, the most important first. Start one on the topic plan.
bp.nextEmptyText: Approve topics on the topic plan to fill this list.
bp.reviewSub: {n} stuck for {d} days or more. Open an article to pass its step.
bp.reviewSubOwn: The writer never passes his own article: someone else takes the step.
bp.reviewEmptyText: Drafts and articles in review show here.
bp.refreshSub: Live articles not edited for {n} days or more. Open one to check its facts, prices and links.
bp.refreshEmptyText: Live articles older than the refresh time show here.
bp.cardText: On: the calendar fills each day only up to the pace — the start pace for the first days, the full pace only while the journal is healthy.
bp.how1: Approve topics on the topic plan; the most important waits on top of “Write next”.
bp.how2: An article passes three steps — proofread, business facts, SEO — each by someone other than its writer.
bp.how3: A finished article takes the next free time on the calendar, only up to today's pace.
bp.how4: If too many articles are sent back, or Google indexes too few, the pace drops to the start by itself.
